nodes.summary: 研究采用交错部署（staggered deployment）设计，利用双重差分（Difference-in-Differences）模型识别 AI 访问的因果影响。为解决异质性处理效应带来的偏差，主要使用 Sun & Abraham (2021) 提出的交互加权估计量。
paragraphs: AI 助手在代理层面逐步 rollout，大部分采用发生在 2020 年 11 月至 2021 年 2 月之间。这种交错的部署时间为因果推断提供了变异来源。
基准回归模型为：y_it = δ_t + α_i + β*AI_it + γ*X_it + ε_it。其中 y_it 是结果变量（如每小时解决数），AI_it 是代理 i 在时间 t 是否访问 AI 的指示变量。模型包含时间固定效应（δ_t）和代理固定效应（α_i）。
由于处理效应可能随时间变化或因采用队列不同而异（例如，后期采用的代理可能适应更快），传统的两向固定效应（TWFE）回归可能产生偏差。
因此，研究首选使用 Sun & Abraham (2021) 提出的交互加权（IW）估计量来分析处理效应的动态变化。该估计量在平行趋势和无预期行为假设下是一致的。
主要生产力指标是每小时解决数（RPH），由平均处理时间、每小时聊天数和解决率共同决定。数据显示，处理后代理的平均处理时间从 40 分钟降至 35 分钟，RPH 显著提升。

3  Deployment, Data, and Empirical Strategy


3.1  AI Model Deployment

The AI assistant we study was gradually rolled out at the agent level after an initial seven-week

randomized pilot featuring 50 agents.12 The deployment was largely uniform across both the data

ﬁrm’s own customer service agents, as well as its outsourced agents.  Figure 2 documents the

progression of deployment among agents who are eventually treated. The bulk of the adoption

occurs between November 2020 and February 2021.


3.2  Summary Statistics

Table 1 provides details on sample characteristics, divided into three groups: agents who are never

given access to the AI tool during our sample period (“never treated”), pre-AI observations for

those who are eventually given access (“treated, pre”), and post-AI observations (“treated, post”).

In total, we observe the conversation text and outcomes associated with 3 million chats by 5,179

agents. Within this, we observe 1.2 million chats by 1,636 agents in the post-AI period. Most agents

in our sample, 83 percent, are located outside the United States, primarily in the Philippines. For

each agent, we observe their assigned manager, tenure, geographic location and ﬁrm information.

   To examine the impacts of this deployment, we construct several key variables, all aggregated

to the agent-month level, which is our primary level of analysis.

   Our primary measure of productivity is resolutions per hour (RPH), the number of chats that

a worker is able to successfully resolve per hour. We consider this measure to be the most eﬀective

summary of a worker’s productivity at the ﬁrm. An agent’s RPH is determined by several factors:

the average time it takes an agent to complete a conversation, the number of conversations they

are able to handle per hour (accounting for multiple simultaneous conversations), and the share of

conversations that are successfully resolved. We measure these individually as, respectively, average

handle time (AHT), chats per hour (CPH), and resolution rate (RR). In addition, we also observe

a measure of customer satisfaction through an agent’s net promoter score (NPS), which is collected

by the ﬁrm from post-call customer surveys.

  12Data from the RCT is included as part of our primary analysis but is not analyzed separately because of its small

We observe these measures for diﬀerent numbers of agents.  In particular, we are able to re-

construct measures of average handle time and chats per hour from our chat level data. Therefore

we observe AHT and CPH measures for all agents in our sample. Measures that involve an un-

derstanding of call quality—resolution rates, and customer satisfaction—are provided at the agent

month level by our data ﬁrm. Because our data outsources most of its customer service functions,

it does not have direct control over this information, which is kept by subcontracted ﬁrms. As a

result, we observe resolution rates and net promoter scores for a subset of agents in our data. This,

in turn, means that we only observe our omnibus productivity measure—resolutions per hour—for

this smaller subset.

   Figure 3 plots the raw distributions of our outcomes for each of the never, pre-, and post-

treatment subgroups. Several of our main results are readily visible in these raw data. In Panels

A through D, we see that post-treatment agents have higher outcomes than both never-treated

agents and pre-treatment agents. In Panel E, we see no discernible diﬀerences in surveyed customer

satisfaction among pre- and post-AI groups.

   Focusing on our main productivity measure, Panel A of Figure 3 and Table 1 show that never-

treated agents resolve an average of 1.7 chats per hour whereas post-treatment agents resolve 2.5

chats per hour. Some of this diﬀerence may be due to diﬀerences in the initial section: treated

agents have higher resolutions per hour prior to AI model deployment (2.0 chats) relative to never

treated agents (1.7). This same pattern appears for other outcomes: chats per hour (Panel C) and

resolution rates (Panel D). Panel B illustrates the clearest pattern with average handle times: both

pre-treatment and never-treated agents had a similar distribution of average handle times, centered

at 40 minutes but post-treatment agents have a lower average handle time of 35 minutes.


3.3  Empirical Strategy

We isolate the causal impact of access to AI recommendations using a standard diﬀerence-in-

diﬀerences regression model:


                                         yit “ δt ` αi ` βtAIit ` γXit ` ϵit                              (1)


Our outcome variables yit capture average handle times, resolution rates, resolutions per hour, and

customer satisfaction scores for agent i in year-month t. Because workers often work only for a

portion of the year, we include only year-month observations for an agent who is actively employed

(e.g. assigned to chats). Our main variable of interest is AIit, an indicator equal to one if agent

i has access to AI recommendations at time t. All regressions include year-month ﬁxed eﬀects δt



                                          11

to control for common, time-varying factors such as tax season or business quarter end.  In our

preferred speciﬁcation, we also include controls for time-invariant agent-level ﬁxed eﬀects αi and

time-varying agent tenure. Standard errors are clustered at the agent or agent-location level.

  A rapidly growing literature has shown that two-way ﬁxed eﬀects regressions deliver consistent

estimates only with strong assumptions about the homogeneity of treatment eﬀects, and may be

biased when treatment eﬀects vary over time or by adoption cohort (Cengiz et al., 2019; de Chaise-

martin and D’Haultfœuille, 2020; Sun and Abraham, 2021; Goodman-Bacon, 2021; Callaway and

Sant’Anna, 2021; Borusyak et al., 2022). For instance, workers may take time to adjust to using the

AI system, in which case its impact in the ﬁrst month may be smaller. Alternatively, the onboarding

of later cohorts of agents may be smoother, so that their treatment eﬀects may be larger.

  We study the dynamics of treatment eﬀects using the interaction weighted (IW) estimator pro-

posed in Sun and Abraham (2021). Sun and Abraham (2021) show that this estimator is consistent

assuming parallel trends, no anticipatory behavior, and cohort-speciﬁc treatment eﬀects that follow

the same dynamic proﬁle.13 In the Appendix, we show that both our main diﬀerences-in-diﬀerences

and event study estimates are similar using robust estimators introduced in de Chaisemartin and

D’Haultfœuille (2020), Borusyak et al. (2022), Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021), and Sun and Abra-

ham (2021), as well as using traditional two-way ﬁxed eﬀects OLS.


4  Results


4.1  Productivity

Table 2 examines the impact of AI model deployment on our primary measure of productivity,

resolutions per hour, using a standard two-way ﬁxed eﬀects model. In Column 1, we show that,

controlling for time and location ﬁxed eﬀects, access to AI recommendations increases the number

of resolutions per hour by 0.47 chats, up 22.2 percent from an average of 2.12.  In Column 2,

we include individual agent ﬁxed eﬀects to account for potential diﬀerences between treated and

untreated agents. In Column 3, we include further controls for time-varying agent tenure. As we

add controls, our eﬀects fall slightly so that, with agent and tenure ﬁxed eﬀects, we ﬁnd that the

deployment of AI increases RPH by 0.30 calls or 13.8 percent. Columns 4 though 6 produce these

same patterns and magnitudes for the log of RPH.

S006.quote:
We study the staggered introduction of a generative AI-based conversational assistant using
data from 5,179 customer support agents. Access to the tool increases productivity, as measured
by issues resolved per hour, by 14 percent on average, with the greatest impact on novice and
low-skilled workers, and minimal impact on experienced and highly skilled workers. We provide
suggestive evidence that the AI model disseminates the potentially tacit knowledge of more able
workers and helps newer workers move down the experience curve. In addition, we show that
AI assistance improves customer sentiment, reduces requests for managerial intervention, and
improves employee retention.

Generative AI and Large Language Models

S102.quote: In recent years, the rapid pace of AI development and public release tools such as ChatGPT,

S103.quote: GitHub Copilot, and DALL-E have attracted widespread attention, optimism, and alarm (The

S104.quote: White House, 2022). These technologies are all examples of “generative AI,” a class of machine

S105.quote: learning technologies that can generate new content—such as text, images, music, or video—by

S106.quote: analyzing patterns in existing data. In this section, we provide background on generative AI as a

S107.quote: technology and discuss its potential economic implications.

S109.quote: In this paper, we focus on an important class of generative AI, large language models (LLMs). At

S110.quote: a high level, LLMs are neural network models designed to process sequential data (Bubeck et al.,

S111.quote: 2023). For instance, an LLM can be trained by giving it access to a large corpus of text (such

S112.quote: as Wikipedia, digitized books, or portions of the Internet) and using that input text to learn to

S113.quote: predict the next word in a sequence, given what has come before. This knowledge of the statistical

S114.quote: co-occurrence of words allows it to generate new text that is grammatically correct and semantically

S116.quote: Though the name implies human language, the same techniques can be used to produce LLMs

S117.quote: that generate other forms of sequential data such as protein sequences, audio, computer code, or

S119.quote: Recent progress in generative AI has been driven by four factors: computing power, earlier

S120.quote: innovations in model architecture, the ability to “pre-train” using large amounts of unlabeled data,

S121.quote:
and reﬁnements in training techniques.4
Model performance depends strongly on scale, which

S122.quote: includes the amount of computing power used for training, the number of model parameters, and

S123.quote: dataset size (Kaplan et al., 2020). Pre-training an LLM requires thousands of GPUs and weeks to

S124.quote: months of dedicated training time. For example, estimates indicate that a single training run for a

S125.quote: GPT-3 model with 175 billion parameters, trained on 300 billion tokens, may cost $5 million dollars

S126.quote: in just computing costs (Li, 2020; Brown et al., 2020).

S127.quote: In terms of model architecture, modern LLMs make use of two earlier key innovations: positional

S128.quote: encoding and self-attention. Positional encodings keep track of the order in which a word occurs

S129.quote: in a given input.5 This allows large bodies of input text to be broken into smaller segments that

S130.quote: can be processed simultaneously without “forgetting” earlier parts of the input (Vaswani et al.,

S131.quote: 2017; Bahdanau et al., 2015). Meanwhile, self-attention assigns importance weights to each word

S132.quote: in the context of the entire input text. Older approaches that assign importance based on word

S133.quote: frequencies that may misrepresent a word’s true semantic importance. These older methods may

S134.quote: also base on semantic content within a small window. In contrast, self-attention enables models to

S135.quote:

et al. (2023); Ouyang et al. (2022).

S136.quote: 5For instance, a model would keep track of “the, 1” instead of only “the” (if “the” was the ﬁrst word in the sentence).

S137.quote: capture long-range semantic relationships within an input text, even when that text is broken up

S138.quote: and processed in parallel (Vaswani et al., 2017).

S139.quote: Second, LLMs can be pre-trained on large amounts of unlabeled data. For instance, GPT is

S140.quote: trained on unlabeled text data, allowing it to learn patterns in human language without explicit

S141.quote:
guidance (Radford and Narasimhan, 2018).
Because unlabeled data is far more prevalent than

S142.quote: labeled data, this allows for LLMs to learn about natural language on a much larger training corpus

S143.quote: (Brown et al., 2020). The resulting model can be used in multiple applications because its training

S144.quote: is not speciﬁc to a particular set of tasks.6

S145.quote: Finally, general-purpose LLMs can be further “ﬁne-tuned” to generate output that matches the

S146.quote: priorities of any speciﬁc setting (Ouyang et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2023). For example, an LLM may

S147.quote: generate several potential responses to a given query, but some of them may be factually incorrect

S148.quote: or biased. To discipline this model, human evaluators can rank these outputs to train a reward

S149.quote: function prioritizes some responses over others. Such reﬁnements can signiﬁcantly improve model

S150.quote: quality but making a general-purpose model better suited to its speciﬁc application (Ouyang et al.,

S151.quote: Together, these innovations have generated meaningful improvements in model performance.

S152.quote: The Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) family of models, in particular, has attracted con-

S153.quote: siderable media attention for their rapidly expanding capabilities.7

The Economic Impacts of Generative AI

S155.quote: Computers have historically excelled at executing pre-programmed instructions, making them par-

S156.quote: ticularly eﬀective at tasks that can be standardized and reduced to explicit rules (Autor, 2014).

S157.quote: Consequently, computerization has had a disproportionate impact on jobs that involve routine

S158.quote: tasks, such as data entry, bookkeeping, and assembly line work, and reducing demand for workers

S159.quote: performing “routine” tasks (Acemoglu and Autor, 2011). At the same time, computerization has

S160.quote: also increased the productivity of workers who possess complementary skills, such as programming,

S161.quote: data analysis, and research. Together, these changes have contributed to increasing wage inequality

S162.quote: in the United States and have been linked to a variety of organizational changes (Katz and Murphy,

S163.quote: 1992; Autor et al., 2003; Michaels et al., 2014; Bresnahan et al., 2002; Baker and Hubbard, 2003).

S164.quote: In contrast, recent advances in AI, particularly those driven by generative AI, suggest that it

S165.quote: is possible for LLMs to perform a variety of non-routine tasks such as software coding, persuasive

S169.quote: an AI pair programmer that generates code suggestions for programmers, has achieved impressive

S170.quote: performance on technical coding questions and generates an average of 46 percent of code among

S171.quote: users (Nguyen and Nadi, 2022; Zhao, 2023). Similarly, services like Elicit and Casetext use LLMs to

S172.quote: ﬁnd and summarize key information in legal documents or research, tasks that were previously con-

S173.quote: sidered non-routine (Elicit, 2023; Casetext, 2023). Since many of these tasks are currently performed

S174.quote: by workers who have either been insulated or beneﬁted from prior waves of technology adoption,

S175.quote: the expansion of generative AI has the potential to shift the relationship between technology, labor

S177.quote: Unlike traditional programming, generative AI does not require explicit instructions as inputs.

S178.quote: Instead, it uses ML to mine vast amounts of human-generated data to recognize patterns, allowing

S179.quote: it to generate, summarize, and make inferences based on those patterns. For instance, if prompted

S180.quote: to provide a cover for a gothic novel, generative AI models will respond with an illustration that is

S181.quote: moody; if asked to write an email denying an employee a raise, generative AI will respond with a

S182.quote: note that is professional; this occurs even though no programmer has instructed the AI model as to

S183.quote: what tone would be appropriate in a given context. The ability to behave “appropriately” cannot

S184.quote: be reduced to a set of rules; instead people learn to do so from experience and apply unconscious

S185.quote: rules in the process. The fact that generative AI models display such skills suggests that they have

S186.quote: the potential to move past what has been termed “Polanyi’s Paradox,” the idea that knowledge is

S187.quote: diﬃcult to codify because individuals perform many tasks they cannot articulate (Polanyi, 1966;

S189.quote: At the same time, LLMs have signiﬁcant limitations. Popular LLM-based tools such as ChatGPT

S190.quote: have been shown to produce false or misleading information in unpredictable ways. While these

S191.quote: models often perform well on speciﬁc tasks in the lab, these concerns have raised questions about

S192.quote: their ability to perform well in more complex real-world settings (Peng et al., 2023a).

Our Setting: LLMs for Customer Support

S195.quote: We study the impact of generative AI in the customer service industry, an area with one the highest

S196.quote: surveyed rates of AI adoption.8 Customer support interactions are important for maintaining a

S197.quote:
8For instance, of the businesses that report using AI, 22 percent use AI in their customer service centers (Chui et
al., 2021).

S198.quote: company’s reputation and building strong customer relationships, yet as in many industries, there

S199.quote: is substantial variation in worker productivity (Berg et al., 2018; Syverson, 2011).

S200.quote: Newer workers are also often less productive and require signiﬁcant training. At the same time,

S201.quote: turnover is high: industry estimates suggest that 60 percent of agents in contact centers9 leave each

S202.quote: year, costing ﬁrms $10,000 to $20,000 dollars per agent (Buesing et al., 2020; Gretz and Jacobson,

S203.quote: 2018). To address these workforce challenges, the average supervisor spends at least 20 hours per

S204.quote: week coaching lower-performing agents (Berg et al., 2018). Faced with variable productivity, high

S205.quote: turnover, and high training costs, ﬁrms are increasingly turning toward AI tools (Chui et al., 2021).

S206.quote: At a technical level, customer support is well-suited for current generative AI tools. From an

S211.quote: problems (“Can you check that caps lock is not on?”). At the same time, they must be attuned to

S212.quote: a customer’s emotional response, making sure to use language that increases the likelihood that a

S213.quote: customer will respond positively (“that wasn’t stupid of you at all! I always forget to check that

S214.quote: too!”). Because customer service conversations are widely recorded and digitized, pre-trained LLMs

S215.quote: can be ﬁne-tuned for customer service using many examples of both successfully and unsuccessfully

S233.quote: Our ﬁrm measures productivity using three metrics that are standard in the customer service

S234.quote: industry: “average handle time,” the average length of time an agent takes to ﬁnish a chat; “resolution

S235.quote: rate,” the share of conversations that the agent can successfully resolve; and “net promoter score,”

S240.quote: Across locations, agents are organized into teams with a manager that provides feedback and

S241.quote: training to agents. Once per week, managers hold one-on-one feedback sessions with each agent.

S242.quote: For example, a manager might share the solution to a new software bug, explain the implication of

S243.quote: a tax change, or suggest how to better manage customer frustration with technical issues. Agents

S244.quote: work individually and the quality of their output does not directly aﬀect others. Agents are paid

S245.quote: an hourly wage and bonuses based on their performance relative to other agents.

S247.quote: The AI system we study uses a generative model system that combines a recent version of GPT

S248.quote: with additional ML algorithms speciﬁcally ﬁne-tuned to focus on customer service interactions. The

S249.quote: system is further trained on a large set of customer-agent conversations that have been labeled with

S250.quote: a variety of outcomes and characteristics: whether the call was successfully resolved, how long it

S251.quote: took to handle the call, and whether the agent in charge of the call is considered a “top” performer

S252.quote: by the data ﬁrm. The AI ﬁrm then uses these data to look for conversational patterns that are

S253.quote: most predictive of call resolution and handle time.

S254.quote: The AI ﬁrm further trains its model using a process similar in spirit to Ouyang et al. (2022) to

S255.quote: prioritize agent responses that express empathy, surface appropriate technical documentation, and

S256.quote: limit unprofessional language. This additional training mitigates some of concerns associated with

S257.quote: relying on LLMs to generate text.

S258.quote: Once deployed, the AI system generates two main types of outputs: 1) real-time suggestions for

S259.quote: how agents should respond to customers and 2) links to the data ﬁrm’s internal documentation for

S260.quote: relevant technical issues. In both cases, recommendations are based on a history of the conversation.

S261.quote: For example, the correct response when a customer says “I can’t track my employee’s hours during

S262.quote: business trips” depends on what version of the data ﬁrm’s software the customer uses. Suppose

S263.quote: the customer has previously mentioned that they are using the premium version. In that case,

S264.quote: they should have access to remote mobile device timekeeping, meaning that the support agents

S265.quote: need to diagnose and resolve a technical issue preventing the software from working. If, however,

S266.quote: the customer stated that they are using the standard version, then the correct solution is for the

S267.quote: customer to upgrade to the premium version in order to access this feature.10

S521.quote: Next, we consider why AI may have these impacts. This section provides evidence from prelim-

S522.quote: inary analysis of the textual content of chat conversations. Our goal is to understand whether and

S523.quote: how AI recommendations change the way agents communicate.

S524.quote: In particular, we are interested in AI model’s ability to encode the potentially tacit knowledge of

S525.quote: high performers: does AI assistance lead lower-skill workers to communicate more like higher-skill

S526.quote: workers? Because tacit knowledge is, by deﬁnition, not something that can be codiﬁed as a set of

S527.quote: rules, we examine the overall textual similarity of conversations rather than looking for the presence

S529.quote: We begin by constructing textual embeddings of agent-customer conversations. These embed-

S530.quote: dings allow us to represent their semantic and stylistic content as a vector so that we can compare

S531.quote: one conversation to another using cosine similarity. Cosine similarity is a widely-used metric for

S532.quote: measuring the similarity of two embeddings. It calculates the cosine of the angle between two n-

S533.quote: dimensional vectors, where values close to 1 indicate similarity (Koroteev, 2021). We form our text

S534.quote: embeddings using all-MiniLM-L6-v2, an LLM that is speciﬁcally intended to capture and cluster

S535.quote: semantic information in order to assess similarity (Hugging Face, 2023). We then compare how an

S536.quote: agent’s conversations change over time (e.g. within-person similarity over time), as well as how high-

S537.quote: and low-skill agents’ conversations compare with each other over time (between-person similarity

S538.quote: at a given point in time).

S542.quote: an eight-week window before deployment and compare it with text from the same-sized window af-

S544.quote: and individual adjustment to the AI model. We exclude messages from the customer, and focus

S545.quote: only on agent-generated language. Then, for each individual agent, we plot textual dissimilarity be-

S546.quote: tween pre- and post-AI conversations as one minus the cosine similarity. The within-person textual

S547.quote: diﬀerence in our data is roughly 0.3, indicating that, on average, agents continue to communicate

S548.quote: similarly after the deployment of the AI model. For context, the sentences “Can you help me with

S549.quote: this logging in?” and “Why is my login not working?” have a cosine similarity of 0.68.

S587.quote: Access to AI assistance may impact workers and the ﬁrm organization as a whole through changes in

S588.quote: work experience, turnover, and task allocation. In this section, we examine some of these outcomes.

S594.quote: attrition among customer service workers (Lee, 2015). It is unclear what impact AI assistants may

S595.quote: have on the tenor of conversations: AI recommendations may help the agent more eﬀectively set the

S596.quote: customer’s expectations or resolve their problem, but customers may react poorly if AI-suggested

S647.quote: Changes in individual worker-level productivity may have broader implications for organizational

S648.quote: workﬂows (Garicano, 2000; Athey et al., 1994; Athey and Stern, 1998). In most ﬁrms, customer

S649.quote: support agents are organized both vertically and horizontally. Vertically, front-line agents try to

S650.quote: resolve customer problems but can seek the help of supervisors when they are unsure of how to

S651.quote: proceed. Customers in our data will sometimes attempt to escalate a conversation by asking to

S652.quote: speak to a manager. This type of request generally occurs when the customer feels the current

S653.quote: agent is not equipped to address their problem or becomes frustrated. Our data ﬁrm, like most

S654.quote: other contact centers, employs designated “escalation agents” to deal with these requests.

S655.quote: Horizontally, agents often represent speciﬁc departments that handle speciﬁc tasks. For example,

S656.quote: some may specialize in technical software issues while others specialize in account management

S657.quote: issues. A customer with a technical issue requiring that their account be upgraded to a premium

S658.quote: product would likely be transferred to a diﬀerent department.

S679.quote: Progress in machine learning opens up a broad set of economic possibilities. Our paper provides

S680.quote: the ﬁrst empirical evidence on the eﬀects of a generative AI tool in a real-world workplace. In

S681.quote: our setting, we ﬁnd that access to AI-generated recommendations increases worker productivity,

S682.quote: improves customer sentiment, and is associated with reductions in employee turnover.

S683.quote: We hypothesize the part of the eﬀect we document is driven by the AI system’s ability to

S684.quote: embody the best practices of high-skill workers in our ﬁrm. These practices may have previously

S685.quote: been diﬃcult to disseminate because they involve tacit knowledge. Consistent with this, we see that

S686.quote: AI assistance leads to substantial improvements in problem resolution and customer satisfaction for

S687.quote: newer- and less-skilled workers, but does not help the highest-skilled or most-experienced workers

S688.quote: on these measures. Analyzing the text of agent conversations, we ﬁnd suggestive evidence that AI

S689.quote: recommendations lead low-skill workers to communicate more like high-skill workers.

S690.quote: Our ﬁndings, and their limitations, point to a variety of directions for future research.

S691.quote: As a potential general-purpose technology, generative AI can and will be deployed in a variety of

S692.quote: ways, and the eﬀects we ﬁnd may not generalize across all ﬁrms and production processes (Eloundou

S693.quote: et al., 2023). For example, our setting has a relatively stable product and set of technical support

S694.quote: questions. In areas where the product or environment is changing rapidly, the relative value of AI

S695.quote: recommendations—trained on historical data—may be diﬀerent.

S696.quote: Our results do not capture potential longer-term impacts on skill demand, job design, wages, or

S697.quote: customer demand. For example, more eﬀective technical support could accelerate the trend towards

S698.quote: contact center agents taking on more complex customer responsibilities, increasing aggregate de-

S699.quote: mand even if agents become more productive (Berg et al., 2018; Korinek, 2022). And over the longer

S700.quote: term, these tools can uncover patterns and insights that may not be documented in formal channels,

S701.quote: changing the way workers are managed or how knowledge is shared within an organization.

S702.quote: Finally, our ﬁndings raise questions about whether and how workers should be compensated for

S703.quote: the data that they provide to AI systems. High-skill workers, in particular, play an important role

S704.quote: in model development but see smaller direct beneﬁts in terms of improving their own productivity.

S705.quote: Given the early stage of generative AI, these and other questions deserve further scrutiny.

nodes.title: AI 系统机制与隐性知识传播
异质性分析：技能偏向型变革
机制证据：经验曲线加速
文本证据：沟通模式的趋同
组织结果：情感分析与留存率
研究局限与适用范围条件

concept-0a234433145240a9.title: 生成式 AI (Generative AI)
concept-0a234433145240a9.lead: 能够生成新内容（如文本、图像）的 AI 系统。
concept-0a234433145240a9.text: 在本文中，生成式 AI 指基于大型语言模型（LLM）的工具，能够分析现有数据中的模式并生成新的响应内容。它与传统编程不同，不需要显式的指令编码，而是从示例中学习。
concept-0a234433145240a9.why: 理解该概念是区分本研究与以往自动化研究的基础，因为生成式 AI 能处理非结构化任务和隐性知识。

concept-9166bf36d4e11321.title: 隐性知识 (Tacit Knowledge)
concept-9166bf36d4e11321.lead: 难以通过语言或文字明确表达的知识，通常通过经验获得。
concept-9166bf36d4e11321.text: 指那些无法轻易编码或指令化的生产过程中的知识。作者假设 AI 系统能够捕捉高技能工人的隐性知识（通过其行为模式），并将其传播给低技能工人，从而缩小技能差距。
concept-9166bf36d4e11321.why: 这是解释为何 AI 主要帮助低技能工人的核心机制假设。

concept-be42c7c54b9d8aaa.title: 微调 (Fine-tuning)
concept-be42c7c54b9d8aaa.lead: 在预训练模型基础上使用特定领域数据进行的额外训练。
concept-be42c7c54b9d8aaa.text: 本研究中，基础 GPT 模型使用了特定的客户 - 代理对话数据进行微调，这些数据标记了解决状态和代理绩效。这使得模型能够学习特定于该技术支持环境的最佳实践，而不仅仅是通用语言模式。
concept-be42c7c54b9d8aaa.why: 解释了为何通用 LLM 能在此特定工作场景中产生高价值建议。

concept-093adf1f9e08a97e.title: 基于人类反馈的优化 (类似 RLHF 的过程)
concept-093adf1f9e08a97e.lead: 调整模型输出以符合人类价值观和特定目标的技术。
concept-093adf1f9e08a97e.text: 文中提到系统经过进一步训练，以优先选择表达同理心、提供准确文档链接并限制不专业语言的回复。这种训练减轻了直接使用 LLM 生成文本的一些担忧（如幻觉或不恰当内容）。
concept-093adf1f9e08a97e.why: 说明了系统如何保证建议的质量和安全性，使其适合企业环境。

concept-87ad284076372608.title: 交错部署 (Staggered Deployment)
concept-87ad284076372608.lead: 处理组在不同时间点陆续接受干预的实验设计。
concept-87ad284076372608.text: 在本研究中，AI 工具不是同时分配给所有代理，而是在一段时间内逐步 rollout。这种设计允许研究者比较同一代理在接收工具前后的表现，以及不同时间接收工具的队列之间的差异，从而构建反事实。
concept-87ad284076372608.why: 这是识别因果效应的关键数据来源，使得双重差分方法可行。

concept-8685206aa781a70e.title: Sun & Abraham (2021) 估计量
concept-8685206aa781a70e.lead: 一种用于处理交错采用双重差分中异质性处理效应的稳健估计方法。
concept-8685206aa781a70e.text: 当处理效应随时间变化或在不同采用队列间存在差异时，传统的双重差分估计量可能不一致。Sun & Abraham (2021) 提出的交互加权估计量通过聚合队列特定的事件时间效应来解决这一问题，前提是满足平行趋势假设。
concept-8685206aa781a70e.why: 该方法确保了在处理效应动态变化复杂的情况下，研究结论的统计可靠性。

concept-07ed60823dc56197.title: 每小时解决量 (Resolutions Per Hour)
concept-07ed60823dc56197.lead: 衡量客服生产力的主要因变量。
concept-07ed60823dc56197.text: 指代理在一小时内成功解决的技术支持问题数量。该指标综合反映了处理速度和多任务处理能力。
concept-07ed60823dc56197.why: 这是本文评估 AI 影响的最关键产出指标，直接对应劳动力经济学中的生产率定义。

concept-beb2726e9b0e94be.title: 意向治疗效应 (Intent-to-Treat)
concept-beb2726e9b0e94be.lead: 本文主要报告的估计策略。
concept-beb2726e9b0e94be.text: 指评估“获得 AI 访问权限”这一事件本身的影响，无论代理实际使用或遵循 AI 建议的频率如何。这避免了因代理选择性使用工具而产生的内生性偏差。
concept-beb2726e9b0e94be.why: 理解此概念有助于明白为何文中数据反映的是‘接入’带来的平均效果，而非‘完美使用’下的理论上限。

concept-ab847cf8a03a7f06.title: 技能五分位 (Skill Quintiles)
concept-ab847cf8a03a7f06.lead: 用于分析异质性效应的代理分类标准。
concept-ab847cf8a03a7f06.text: 作者根据代理在 AI 部署前一个季度的三个关键指标（平均处理时长、解决率、客户满意度）计算综合技能指数，并在每个公司 - 月份内将代理分为五组。Q1 代表技能最低的 20%，Q5 代表技能最高的 20%。
concept-ab847cf8a03a7f06.why: 这种动态分组确保了比较是在同等相对水平的代理之间进行，排除了公司间固有差异的干扰，是识别‘技能偏向型’技术变革的关键设计。

concept-50a77f6bb0e6795c.title: 经验曲线 (Experience Curve)
concept-50a77f6bb0e6795c.lead: 描述绩效随工作时间积累的演变路径。
concept-50a77f6bb0e6795c.text: 在本文中，指代理的生产力（每小时解决量）随其在公司任职月数增加而变化的轨迹。传统上，这是一条平缓上升的曲线，代表‘熟能生巧’的过程。AI 的作用是使这条曲线变得更陡峭，缩短了达到熟练水平所需的时间。
concept-50a77f6bb0e6795c.why: 这是理解 AI 如何替代或加速人力资本积累的核心概念。它解释了为何 AI 对新手价值最大——因为它压缩了新手最需要漫长的‘试错学习’阶段。

concept-a9e5ecf658d9f02e.title: 余弦相似度 (Cosine Similarity)
concept-a9e5ecf658d9f02e.lead: 衡量两个向量在多维空间中方向一致性的指标。
concept-a9e5ecf658d9f02e.text: 在本文本分析中，余弦相似度用于量化两段对话文本在语义和风格上的接近程度。值为 1 表示完全相同，0 表示正交（无相关性）。研究者用它来比较不同技能水平员工的语言向量。
concept-a9e5ecf658d9f02e.why: 理解该指标是解读“语言趋同”结论的基础，它证明了变化不仅是词汇的重复，而是整体沟通风格的靠近。

concept-96e15d3b33b7edc8.title: 隐性知识 (Tacit Knowledge)
concept-96e15d3b33b7edc8.lead: 难以通过书面规则或公式明确表达的知识，通常通过经验获得。
concept-96e15d3b33b7edc8.text: 在客户服务中，隐性知识包括如何安抚愤怒客户、何时使用幽默或非正式语气等微妙技巧。文章假设 AI 模型通过学习高绩效者的数据，将这些难以编码的经验转化为具体的建议，从而传递给低技能员工。
concept-96e15d3b33b7edc8.why: 这是解释为何低技能员工能迅速提升表现且语言风格发生改变的核心理论机制。

concept-0818efd0311e1d8d.title: 情感分析 (Sentiment Analysis)
concept-0818efd0311e1d8d.lead: 利用自然语言处理技术识别文本中的情绪倾向（如积极、消极）。
concept-0818efd0311e1d8d.text: 本研究使用 SiEBERT 模型，该模型经过产品评论和推文等多种数据集的微调，能够评分从 -1 到 1 的情感值。研究者分别计算客服人员和客户的情感得分，以评估 AI 对互动质量的影响。
concept-0818efd0311e1d8d.why: 这是量化“客户满意度”和“员工情绪劳动”的关键技术手段，解释了为何 AI 能改善软性指标。

concept-cc8004fca5617322.title: 流失率 (Attrition)
concept-cc8004fca5617322.lead: 指员工离开组织的比率，是衡量工作满意度和组织健康的重要指标。
concept-cc8004fca5617322.text: 在客服中心，高流失率通常与高压、低胜任感和情绪耗竭有关。文章发现 AI 辅助显著降低了新员工的流失率，暗示工具可能通过降低认知负荷或提供即时支持，缓解了新手常见的挫败感。
concept-cc8004fca5617322.why: 连接了技术干预与人力资源成本，展示了 AI 在经济效率之外的管理价值。

concept-37aa089890367534.title: 意向治疗分析 (Intent-to-Treat, ITT)
concept-37aa089890367534.lead: 一种分析方法，按初始分配的组别（如是否获得 AI 权限）评估效果，无论受试者实际执行情况如何。
concept-37aa089890367534.text: 文章主要报告的是 ITT 效应，即只要员工获得了 AI 访问权，无论他们是否真的使用了建议，都计入处理组。这反映了政策实施的真实效果。随后，作者专门分析了“依从性”以探讨实际使用程度与回报的关系。
concept-37aa089890367534.why: 区分 ITT 和依从性分析对于理解 AI 的实际潜力和政策落地效果至关重要。ITT 显示了“提供工具”的价值，而依从性分析揭示了“使用工具”的边际收益。

concept-4d80cd2e2047a138.title: 基于收益的选择 (Selection on Gains)
concept-4d80cd2e2047a138.lead: 一种偏差来源，指那些能从干预中获得最大收益的人最有可能去执行该干预。
concept-4d80cd2e2047a138.text: 在解释依从度与生产力的正相关时，作者提出这可能不仅是“听从建议导致高效”，也可能是“那些最能从 AI 中获益的员工更倾向于听从建议”。这种内生性使得因果推断变得复杂。
concept-4d80cd2e2047a138.why: 提醒读者注意观察到的强相关性（高依从=高产出）不一定完全是因果关系，可能存在自我选择机制。

concept-14f45bc0417008c2.title: 隐性知识转移 (Tacit Knowledge Transfer)
concept-14f45bc0417008c2.lead: 指难以通过书面文档形式化，需通过观察或实践传递的专业技能。
concept-14f45bc0417008c2.text: 在本文中，生成式 AI 被假设能够体现高技能员工的最佳实践，这些实践通常包含隐性知识，此前难以传播（pdf-ac0a4e183aa6f936-p23-b8, pdf-ac0a4e183aa6f936-p23-b9）。AI 通过将这些隐性模式转化为显性推荐，帮助低技能员工模仿高技能员工的沟通方式（pdf-ac0a4e183aa6f936-p23-b13）。
concept-14f45bc0417008c2.why: 理解此概念是解释为何 AI 能显著提升低技能员工表现，而对高技能员工影响有限的核心机制。

concept-2f38b5201c5608cf.title: 通用技术情境依赖性 (GPT Context Dependency)
concept-2f38b5201c5608cf.lead: 通用技术（如电力、AI）虽应用广泛，但其具体经济效应高度依赖于部署环境和互补性投资。
concept-2f38b5201c5608cf.text: 作者指出生成式 AI 是一种潜在的通用技术，但其在不同公司和生产流程中的效果可能不同（pdf-ac0a4e183aa6f936-p23-b15, pdf-ac0a4e183aa6f936-p23-b16）。特别是在环境快速变化时，基于历史数据的模型价值会受限，这表明技术效果并非普遍恒定，而是依赖于具体的组织情境和互补性流程（pdf-ac0a4e183aa6f936-p4-b24, pdf-ac0a4e183aa6f936-p23-b19）。
concept-2f38b5201c5608cf.why: 此概念解释了为何不能将本研究的特定结果简单外推至所有行业，强调了环境稳定性作为关键边界条件的重要性。
